chapter: Kansas City, Omaha and Lloyd Hunter
title: Stuck in a blizzard near Shelby, Nebraska
summary: In a panel bus with no heat control, the band hit a snowdrift at 32 below, and Gus walked two miles seeking help.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: The only time I got stranded was in Shelby, Nebraska with Lloyd Hunter's band, and that was on account of a big snowdrift. We were going to Shelby that night, and they had a blizzard, 32 below zero.

On the road, see. We were about -- well, country miles, we were about eight miles from town, from Shelby, because they were driving, the driver got tired of driving, so we would all switch about, and drive. So I was driving. And the snow was drifting across the highway and you couldn't see as far as from here to that wall.

And I saw this snowdrift right across the road, so I stepped on it and hit it, to go through it, you see. And I hit it and it was like hitting up against a brick wall. I got stuck. We couldn't move. And lucky we couldn't, we couldn't have gone any farther, anyway.
Because the snow cleared away from blowing, and there was about 12 cars ahead of us, see.
And they were all stuck, too.

Everybody -- we had this panel bus, where the heat ran right between your legs, all the way back. It was a pipe ran all the way down inside. We had two rows of seats, two on this side, two on this side, standard the bus.
And so when you get in the bus, you have this (inaudible).

Heat between your legs, running down there. And if you to sleep and your foot hit that exhaust pipe running through the bus, then you'll smell something. Somebody would say, 'Get your foot off the heater.' And we ended up with pants legs burned and all like that.
But we got out of the bus. So I got out and I said, 'Well, I'll go and see if I can find a house or something.'
I had one of those big camelhair coats that they was wearing during the time.
And so I walked for about two miles up the road, I couldn't find anybody so I came back.
Two miles in all the snow and temperature?
